This is what /opt is serving — an update pulls whatever :latest is now, and bb drift says what a checkout has changed since.

Project settings

Everything this project does off this box goes here — its containers, builds, tests, CI and emulation. What it can build is what is installed on that node (the Tools tab adds to it); an ssh node without an agent hosts containers only. Existing containers stay where they were made.
Run with sh -c in the snapshot's root on the node. Files matching the outputs come back into dist/ with a note of what built them.

New container

Checked by compose itself before it is saved. Relative bind sources resolve against this container's own data directory, which both this container and the daemon can see.
Read by the compose file above as ${VAR}. Kept beside it in /config, never in a project.

Send to Docker manager

Defaults to this project's node from its settings dialog; an instance stays bound to the node it was created on.

Deleted projects

Deleting a project moves it to .trash under the projects share. Its notebook — the roadmap, the bugs, the memories — is left where it is, so putting one back brings all of it with it.
